key_insight: A controllable 4D cardiac MRI generator separates anatomy from motion to synthesize anatomically consistent cine sequences for data augmentation.
clinical_relevance: Synthetic 4D cardiac MRI can help improve segmentation models when annotated data are limited or scanners differ across sites.
method: Semi-supervised VAE learns compact anatomy representations and predicts aligned segmentation masks.
Cascaded latent diffusion generates static subject anatomy from clinical priors, then adds residual motion over time.
Anatomy and motion are disentangled to preserve temporal coherence across the 4D sequence.
evidence_signal: Across multiple datasets, the method showed strong anatomy controllability (Pearson r > 0.8) and temporal coherence (FVD = 288.08), and augmented training improved nnU-Net segmentation performance in cross-vendor tests.
watch_item: Synthetic data may generalize unevenly if clinical priors, scanner characteristics, or motion patterns differ from the target deployment setting.
paper_title: Anatomy-Guided Residual Motion Diffusion for Controllable 4D Cardiac MRI Synthesis
